suggestions.description: Add proper section headers and organize instructions into a logical workflow. This creates a standard README pattern.
suggestions.before:
$ mkdir ~/Hello-WorldCreates a directory...
$ cd ~/Hello-WorldChanges the current...
$ git initSets up...
suggestions.after:
## Getting Started

### 1. Create Project Directory
```bash
$ mkdir ~/Hello-World
```
Creates a directory for your project called "Hello-World" in your user directory.

### 2. Navigate to Directory
```bash
$ cd ~/Hello-World
```
Changes the current working directory to your newly created directory.

### 3. Initialize Git Repository
```bash
$ git init
```
Initialized empty Git repository in /Users/your_user_directory/Hello-World/.git/

### 4. Create README
```bash
$ touch README
```
suggestions.benefits: Creates a standard README structure with clear sections and numbered steps. Users can follow a logical workflow and navigate the documentation easily.

refactorings.summary: The README patch lacks proper markdown formatting for shell commands and descriptions. Commands are concatenated without separation, making them difficult to read and copy. Four significant refactoring opportunities identified: (1) add code blocks and line breaks to separate commands from descriptions, (2) distinguish command output from commands, (3) use proper markdown heading syntax, and (4) add section headers and numbered steps for better organization.

recommendations.description: Add proper markdown formatting with code blocks for shell commands. Commands and descriptions are currently concatenated on the same line, making the README difficult to read and preventing users from easily copying commands.

Organize instructions into a logical workflow with section headers and numbered steps (e.g., '## Getting Started' with '### 1. Create Project Directory'). This follows standard README patterns and improves user navigation.

Add notes about cross-platform compatibility. The instructions assume a Unix/macOS environment (using ~ directory expansion). Provide alternatives or clarifications for Windows users who may have different directory structures.
Use proper markdown syntax for the title (change 'Hello World!' to '# Hello World!') to create a proper document hierarchy and improve semantic structure.
Distinguish expected command output (like 'Initialized empty Git repository...') from commands by placing it in a separate code block or clearly labeled section.
